headline: Microchip and Navitas have unveiled a compact power-supply design that steps 800 volts down to 6 volts for future AI servers, with efficiency figures that are still the makers' own targets.
score_reason: Lowered from 4: the design was announced on 5 Oct 2026 and we carried it on 6 Oct, igor'sLAB's added analysis is useful but no independent test exists.
importance_line: What changed is a closer look at a design announced a week ago, not a launch, which matters first to data-centre operators, whose power losses add up across thousands of AI chips, then to Microchip and Navitas, and the doubt is that the 96% efficiency is a target with no independent measurement and a reference design is not yet a product.
summary: The hardware site igor'sLAB reports, on the basis of a 5 Oct 2026 announcement by Microchip Technology and Navitas Semiconductor, that the two chipmakers have built a reference design, a ready-made blueprint for other engineers, that turns 800-volt direct current into 6 volts for AI servers using gallium nitride transistors, a chip material that switches fast with comparatively low losses, and will show it at the OCP Global Summit in San Jose on 12 to 15 Oct. New since our 6 Oct 2026 edition, igor'sLAB stresses that the 96% peak efficiency is the makers' own target with no independent measurements yet, and that 'direct' conversion does not necessarily mean one step, since it joins an 800-to-50-volt stage and a 50-to-6-volt stage in one unit.
notes: Read in full (fulltext). igor'sLAB's review rests on the Microchip and Navitas press release, which was not read; the 6 Oct 2026 edition carried the announcement from Semiconductor Today. Part of the article is the reviewer's own opinion.
